| [CASE-340](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-340.md) | Small DeGroot groups, wrong consensus | The audit's sketch for [QUESTION-184](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-184.md), checked against Golub and Jackson's definitions ([LIT-999](../../../record/literature.d/LIT-999.md), reread 2026-11-22) and computed exactly. n agents in m = n/k closed groups of k = ⌈√(ln n)⌉, equal weights inside each group, independent Bernoulli(1/2) signals. Under Theorem 3 every influence weight is 1/k, which tends to 0; under Definition 3 the society is wise only if the largest deviation over all agents tends to 0 in probability. The chance that some group's consensus is exactly 0 or 1, missing the truth by 1/2, is 1 − (1 − 2^(1−k))^m, which tends to 1: 0.97 at n = 10, 0.9999 at n = 100, and 1 to six places from n = 10^4. A DeGroot iteration on a three-group matrix with transient members confirms Theorem 3's per-group normalization, and a Monte Carlo run agrees with the exact formula. With three groups, or with groups of size (ln n)², the same probability tends to 0. The wording is the assistant's (Claude, in this session); adopting it is the owner's call. | Proposed |

Restriction costs 99 [95, 103] units of needless protection more under success feedback than under independent evaluation. An independent audit lets 66 % of runs leave. A protected investigator corrects the belief within a median 6 steps, yet protection outlasts it in 87 % of runs, the regime [CASE-153](../../../record/cases.d/CASE-153.md) asked for. Every regime still protects when danger returns. The case's own check comes out against the authority state: under success feedback its update is the habit of protecting, and a habit of matched memory reproduces the responses to belief correction, authority reset and restored evidence. Only interventions on the evaluation tell the two apart. The phase boundary lies near sentry strength κ = 1.25–1.5 and moves with the assumed switching hazard.
